thread:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: ↑ Error rate and packet loss detected from private interconnects in GCP europe-west4 affecting multiple Private deployments with on-prem peers. Autoscale/ingress unaffected for hosted; private VPC peering and interconnect circuits seeing asymmetric paths and intermittent BGP withdraws.

Mike (on-call): I'm up. Seeing ~30% packet loss on control plane for a subset of routes, and customers reporting TCP timeouts. Taking ownership.

Liz (Support): Multiple enterprise customers (acct: AcmeCorp, FinX) reported 500/timeout spikes since ~07:20 UTC. Support triage shows calls to private endpoints failing; public hosted API unaffected.

Ana (SRE): Confirming metrics: dataplane error spike at 07:19 UTC egress to on-prem prefixes. Cloud-router logs show repeated BGP flap to peer-asn 64521.

Julia (NetEng): Can you paste the cloud-router syslog snippets? I'll check BGP session flips and whether it's an upstream fabric issue.

Mike (on-call): Pasting relevant logs:```\nMay 03 07:18:59 cloud-router-1 bgp[1234]: neighbor 10.10.10.1 (peer-as 64521) state Active -> Connect
May 03 07:19:01 cloud-router-1 bgp[1234]: neighbor 10.10.10.1 state Connect -> Active
May 03 07:19:30 cloud-router-1 kernel: Rcvd ICMP redirect from 35.200.5.2 for 10.1.0.0/16
May 03 07:20:02 cloud-router-1 bgp[1234]: neighbor 10.10.10.1 (peer-as 64521) state Established -> Idle
```

Julia (NetEng): ICMP redirect is suspicious — suggests asymmetric routing inside GCP fabric or towards the customer's edge. I'm opening a ticket with GCP NOC (case GCP-xxxxx).

Raja (Customer Eng): I've messaged AcmeCorp support contact and FinX SEs: telling them we're investigating and will provide workaround. They want ETA.

Ana (SRE): Immediate mitigation thought: we can program a temporary static route on the private VM NACLs to prefer cross-region egress via europe-west1 (secondary) where interconnect looks stable. That requires coordination with Private VPC owners.

Mike (on-call): Trying an internal quick traceroute from a failing host to on-prem prefix:```\ntraceroute to 10.254.10.0 (10.254.10.0), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.128.0.1  0.2 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  35.200.5.2  3.1 ms  3.0 ms  3.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.1  25.6 ms  26.0 ms  25.7 ms
```

Julia (NetEng): hop 2 (35.200.5.2) is one of GCP egress nodes; the *s after that fit asymmetric forwarding. GCP is likely rebalancing/losing next-hop. Opened GCP SR and flagged as impacting on-prem interconnects.

incident-bot: Incident declared P1 — paging on-call escalation. Page sent to SRE rotation and NetEng.

Liz (Support): Customer-facing status sent to affected customer list: short note with workaround request (switch to public endpoints or standby failover). Some customers cannot use public endpoints.

Ana (SRE): I'm going to spin up a temporary cross-region NAT and route private egress for a small canary customer (FinX) to europe-west1 to see if it stabilizes. Will monitor latency and errors.

Mike (on-call): Before changing routing, can we try toggling BFD timers and flap dampening on the cloud-router? If it's an upstream jitter, dampening might reduce withdraw churn. Julia?

Julia (NetEng): We don't have control of vendor BFD on GCP side; cloud-router exposes limited knobs. GCP NOC suggested disabling route reflector for these prefixes and using direct import policies. I'm coordinating details with them.

Ana (SRE): Canary now: created a policy-based route for FinX prefix to egress via europe-west1 NAT. Monitor shows errors drop from 42% -> 5% within 90s. Looks promising.

Raja (Customer Eng): FinX confirms calls restored to private endpoint via the temporary route. They want a workaround timeline.

Oliver (PM): What's customer impact breadth? How many customers on Private in europe-west4? Need to quantify for comms and CSM alert.

Liz (Support): Quick list: 12 Private deployments with on-prem interconnects in europe-west4, 3 showing immediate errors, 4 with intermittent warnings. I'll export a CSV and share.

Mike (on-call): Action plan: 1) Work with GCP NOC for root cause and fix (SR). 2) For affected customers, offer temporary cross-region routing to europe-west1 (automated playbook), or fail over to public endpoints. 3) Prepare a post-incident RCA and note.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation acknowledged by Ana (SRE).

Julia (NetEng): GCP NOC update: "We see ECMP inconsistency on a subset of egress nodes, causing asymmetric flow. Rolling patch to egress fleet in europe-west4, estimated 45-60min to ramp." Ticket ID: GCP-12345678.

Ana (SRE): We'll coordinate a rolling validation. Can we schedule automated traffic diversion (per-tenant) so we don't need manual routes per customer? If yes, we can reduce blast radius and provide quick fix.

Mike (on-call): I can trigger the per-tenant diversion script for the 3 customers in immediate impact. Initiating now.

Mike (on-call): Done for AcmeCorp, FinX, and BetaPayments. Monitoring shows steady state after diversion. AcmeCorp reports restored, BetaPayments still intermittent but improving.

Liz (Support): Sending updated customer message: we've implemented temporary egress to europe-west1 for affected customers; GCP is remediating underlying fabric, we'll provide updates every 30m.

Julia (NetEng): GCP NOC patch progress: 20% nodes completed, observed reduction in withdraws for patched nodes. Next update in ~15m.

Ana (SRE): Handing off on-call to Mike in 30m. I'll prepare runbook notes and add entries to the incident timeline.

Mike (on-call): Acknowledged handoff. Leaving watch on remediation; will escalate if withdrawals resurge.

incident-bot: Note: on-call handoff recorded — Ana -> Mike (07:50 UTC).

(35 minutes later)

Julia (NetEng): GCP confirms patch ramp finished. Withdraw churn normalized ~07:56 UTC. They've closed the SR pending our confirmation.

Mike (on-call): Monitoring stats: packet loss back to baseline, BGP sessions stable. Rolling back temporary diversions to test normal path for one customer (FinX).

FinX (via Raja): FinX confirms traffic is fine on normal path after rollback.

Mike (on-call): Rolling back diversions for all three customers now.

Liz (Support): Final customer message: underlying GCP egress fabric in europe-west4 experienced intermittent ECMP inconsistency causing asymmetric routing and packet loss to some on-prem peers. We implemented temporary per-tenant egress diversion while GCP patched their egress nodes. Services are restored; we're compiling RCA.

Ana (SRE): RCA draft notes: cause: ECMP inconsistency on a subset of GCP europe-west4 egress nodes resulting in asymmetric forwarding -> BGP withdraws and ICMP redirects. Impact: Private on-prem-connected deployments had intermittent TCP failures and increased 5xx rates. Mitigation: temporary per-tenant egress diversion to europe-west1 and coordination with GCP NOC patch. Next steps: automate diversion playbook, add health checks to detect BGP withdraw spike, update runbooks, customer postmortem.

Oliver (PM): Please add timeline and affected customer list to the RCA. Also include remediation options: (1) configurable cross-region failover, (2) multi-region interconnect for critical customers, (3) UI to trigger per-tenant diversion.

Mike (on-call): Closing incident; monitoring for 2 hours. Will file postmortem and assign owners.

incident-bot: Incident status: RESOLVED (service restored) - P1 closed at 08:05 UTC.

Ana (SRE): Thanks team. I'll write up the postmortem and link to this thread.

Raja (Customer Eng): Sending follow-up emails to all impacted accounts now.

Liz (Support): Adding notes to customer tickets and CSMs.

Mike (on-call): Good job everyone.
